_about: Every number here is an ASSUMPTION made for the Phase 1 model, not a rule from the Rules of Play. Each has a unit and a reason. Change them here; nothing in the engine hard-codes these values. Run analyses at more than one setting before trusting a conclusion.

tick_seconds.why: Resolution of the round-based loop. Melee exchanges and incantation progress are resolved once per tick.

speech_words_per_second.why: Incantation time = words x repetitions / this rate. 3.5 words/s is about 210 words a minute: a practiced player reciting a memorized, repeated incantation, still audible at 20' with no two-second gaps. Was 2.5 (150 wpm, ordinary conversation), which made a Heal 16 s and a Magic Ball 10 s and left 6th-level players barely better than 1st-level ones (face-validity check 'level': 0.555 at 2.5, 0.683 at 3.5, 0.733 at 4.5 words/s).

charge_incantation_words.why: Counted from the Charge Incantation in rules/magic-states-effects/mechanics-and-definitions.md. Listed here so charge time uses the same speech rate.

sd.why: Player fighting skill is drawn from Normal(0, sd). Scenarios can widen or narrow the spread.

logit_per_sd.why: How strongly a one-sd skill gap moves the chance of landing a hit.

base_hit_per_second.why: Chance an attacker lands a valid hit on one engaged opponent in one second, equal skill, no shield.

shield_logit.why: Larger shields make the bearer harder to hit.

gang_logit_per_extra_attacker.why: Each extra attacker on the same defender makes each attacker more likely to land a hit.

wounded_leg_logit.why: A kneeling or posting player is easier to hit.

wounded_weapon_arm_logit.why: Attacking with the off hand after the weapon arm is wounded.

no_weapon_attack_scale.why: A player whose melee weapon is destroyed cannot attack until it is repaired (no backup weapon modeled).

hit_location_weights.why: Where landed melee and projectile hits strike.

great_weapon_share.why: Share of shield-less players of classes allowed All Melee who use a two-handed Great weapon (Armor Breaking + Shield Crushing per rules/weapon-types-shields-equipment.md).

shield_use_share.why: Share of players allowed a shield who carry one (their largest allowed size).

stunned_logit.why: A Stunned player cannot defend, so hits on them land far more often.

weak_weapon_logit.why: Magic Users and Archers fighting with a dagger, staff or short weapon.

p_shield_struck_on_miss.why: When an attack with Shield Crushing misses a shield bearer, this often it struck the shield instead (three hits destroy it).

p_engage_per_second.why: Chance a free melee player reaches an enemy in one second (non-spatial stand-in for movement).

backline_factor.why: Casters and archers stay back, so enemies reach them at this fraction of the normal rate.

p_disengage_per_second.why: Chance an engaged pair breaks apart in a second without a death.

caster_weight_when_choosing_melee_target.why: Fighters slightly prefer to go after reachable casters.

p_in_range.why: Chance the intended target is within the ability's range when the caster wants to cast. Checked when the incantation starts.

p_ally_nearby_for_touch.why: Chance a chosen friendly target is close enough for Touch or Other.

p_interrupt_on_armor_hit.why: A caster struck on armor while incanting moves their feet or loses the incantation this often. Wounds, death and action-preventing states always interrupt (rules: feet may not move; Magic Users need an empty hand).

engaged_casting_allowed.why: Policies do not start non-Self incantations while engaged in melee.

magic_ball_p_hit.why: Chance a thrown Magic Ball strikes its target.

magic_ball_retrieve_seconds.why: Time to pick thrown balls back up once none are in hand.

arrow_p_hit.why: Chance an arrow strikes its target.

arrow_shot_seconds.why: Nock, draw and aim time per shot. Arrows are Armor Breaking (rules/weapon-types-shields-equipment.md).

thrown_p_hit.why: Chance a thrown weapon (javelin, rock) strikes. Not yet used by Phase 1 policies.

rejoin_seconds.why: Time from respawning at base to rejoining the fight. Enchantments can be cast during this time.

pregame_prep_seconds.why: Time at the start of a game when players at base cast enchantments before fighting.

look_the_part_share.why: Share of players awarded Look The Part.

archetype_share.why: Share of 6th-level players who consider an Archetype at all. Which one, if any, is then chosen by value (sim/policies/buy.py): the Archetype is taken only when the build it allows, plus what it adds, beats the build without it. Was a coin flip followed by a uniform pick.

magic_user_copy_cap.why: Magic Users buy at most this many copies of a spell whose Max is not listed.

spell_taste_sd.why: Magic Users multiply each spell's usefulness score by a personal taste factor exp(sd x N(0,1)) before buying by score per point (sim/policies/buy.py). Real players of the same class and level buy different lists. Kept narrow so core picks stay near-universal (Heal, Force Bolt); the long tail comes from favorite_spells. With no spread every Healer of a level bought the identical list and a third of the purchasable, modeled abilities were never held in 1,000 games.

favorite_spells.why: Favorite spells a 6th-level Magic User buys one copy of first, drawn uniformly among the spells they can buy that help their side in the engine: the spell a player builds around because they like it, whatever the usefulness score says. Scales with level (one at 1st, round(3 x level / 6) after), because a 1st-level player has five points and few spells to choose from. Gives every purchasable spell a real chance of being held, so ablation can measure it, while the rest of the list follows usefulness.

armor_worn_share.why: Share of players allowed armor who wear their class maximum on every location (the rest wear none).

revive_priority.why: Support casters try to return dead allies to life before anything else.

p_use_offensive_ability_when_free.why: Chance a free martial player with a usable offensive ability casts it instead of closing to melee.

self_insubstantial_seconds.why: How long a player stays in a self-imposed Insubstantial state (Blink etc.) before returning.

forced_move_seconds.why: How long Shove/Push/keep-away style effects keep a player out of melee when the rule gives no duration.

p_charge_when_safe.why: Chance an unengaged player with a spent chargeable ability starts the Charge incantation.

p_enchant_ally_on_field.why: Chance a free enchanter tries to enchant an unenchanted ally on the field (rather than only at base).

abandon_cast_when_attacked.why: A player attacked in melee mid-incantation or mid-Charge stops and defends unless the incantation completes this second. Standing still and talking while being hit is how a veteran caster gets killed; they break off and fight or back away.

max_field_charge_seconds.why: Longest Charge a caster starts while enemies are on the field (about Charge x3 at 3.5 words/s). Longer ones (Charge x5 is 40 s, x10 is 80 s) wait for a lull with no enemy on the field; fighters and archers Charge only in a lull. Standing still for over a minute mid-battle costs more than the recharged use is worth.

song_switch_horizon_seconds.why: How far ahead a Bard looks when deciding to switch songs (sim/policies/songs.py): about how long a battlefield situation (an engagement, an enemy caster in range) lasts before it changes. Switching ends the current song and leaves the Bard silent for the new song's incantation (2 s for most), so the new song must win over this horizon after paying for that: U_new x (H - t) > U_now x H. At 20 s a 2 s song must be about 11% better, which stops a Bard flipping between two songs of near-equal use. Shorter horizons make switching rarer.

song_switch_min_gain.why: Least a Bard must gain to start or switch a song (sim/policies/songs.py): over song_switch_horizon_seconds, the new song after its silent incantation must be worth this much more than keeping the current one, in value points (value_per_threat_second converts). About an Insult's worth. Without it a Bard on a large team flipped between songs of utility 0.11 and 0.14 as single enemies stepped in and out of melee (a 27% jump but a 0.2-point gain); 30% of skald switches were undone within 20 s.

value_per_threat_second.why: Exchange rate between situational utility (sim/policies/utility.py, in threat units) and the fixed usefulness score (sim/policies/value.py), used when a Bard weighs casting another spell against the song its incantation ends. An enemy whose threat a song answers acts about once every 10-20 s, and what it would do is worth about 5-8 points (Stun 6, a wound 5), so one threat unit of song is worth roughly 0.3-0.8 points a second. With a song of utility 1, an 8 s Stun (6 points) costs 5 points of song and is cast; a 3 s Insult (1 point) costs 2.5 and is held.

max_seconds.why: Hard time cap. Games at the cap are scored by remaining lives or kills.

level_weights.why: Placeholder level mix until ORK attendance data is available.

class_weights.why: Placeholder: uniform class mix until ORK data is available.

space._about: Phase 2 stage 1: the field (sim/engine/space.py), used only with --space on. The value calibration (sim/data/value-calibration.json) was measured with space off, and its staleness fingerprint leaves this group out (sim/policies/calibration.py), so editing it does not make the calibration stale.

tick_seconds.why: Tick length on the field. Movement at a run covers 2 m a tick, a little more than melee reach, so a charging fighter can't pass through a reach circle between ticks. Incantations and Charges still count in whole seconds; per-second chances (melee hits, policy rates) are converted to per-tick chances.

decide_seconds.why: How often each player's brain (the policies' decide) chooses what to do on the field: once a second, as in Phase 1, staggered across players so half decide on each tick. Movement, engagement, melee and incantations resolve every tick. Keeps the policies' per-second rates (policy.p_charge_when_safe and the like) as they are, and the run time close to Phase 1's.

field_length_m.why: Length of the rectangle between the two bases (a medium park field). Respawned players walk back over it, so rejoin time grows with it.

field_width_m.why: Width of the field. No obstacles or terrain in stage 1.

walk_speed_mps.why: Ordinary walking pace: taking position, the line's advance, walking back from base. From base to midfield (30 m) takes about 21 s, close to Phase 1's respawn.rejoin_seconds (20 s).

run_speed_mps.why: A jog in armor and garb on grass, kept up over a fight: charging, retreating, a medic reaching the wounded. Everyone runs at the same speed; a sprint (6-7 m/s) isn't sustained.

hobble_speed_mps.why: A player with a wounded leg and no living enemy within 20' may hobble: 'move slowly, take no more than one step per second, and drag a leg' (combat-rules.md, Hit Locations note 6). About half a metre a step.

crawl_speed_mps.why: A player with a wounded leg and a living enemy within 20' kneels (the knee may be lifted briefly to move, note 4a) or posts (the wounded foot may not move, note 4b): moving on the knees at most.

touch_m.why: Touch and Other: 'any physical contact ... or placing one's hand within six inches of the target' (mechanics-and-definitions.md, Range): six inches plus an arm's reach.

reach_m.why: Melee reach by weapon, hand to tip plus a lean: a Magic User's or archer's dagger or short weapon, a fighter's long sword, a two-handed Great weapon. Weapon types beyond Great weapons aren't modeled (all fighters carry 'standard').

throw_range_m.why: Farthest a Magic Ball is thrown at a player. Stage 1 keeps the flat projectiles.magic_ball_p_hit inside this range; the distance curve is stage 2.

bow_range_m.why: Farthest an arrow (normal or Specialty) is shot at a player. Stage 1 keeps the flat projectiles.arrow_p_hit inside this range.

deploy_depth_m.why: Each team forms within this distance of its base end before the game: line fighters on a line at this depth, everyone else behind them.

base_zone_m.why: Line fighters don't charge or start a melee with a player standing within this distance of their own base end, and a formation line stops short of it (a player attacked there may still strike back). A common battlegame convention against camping a base, and the field's stand-in for Phase 1, where a respawned player was off the field for respawn.rejoin_seconds. Without it, a winning team stood on the losing team's base and killed each player as they respawned.

line_spacing_m.why: Lateral spacing between line fighters in their team's line: about a weapon's length each side.

charge_distance_m.why: A line fighter charges (runs at the enemy it can reach soonest) when an enemy is this close; the line walks forward in formation until then. About two seconds at a run.

retreat_trigger_m.why: A caster, healer or archer backs off at a run, and starts no incantation, while a free enemy line fighter is this close (20'): a charging fighter covers it in about 1.5 s, less than most incantations.

preferred_distance_m.why: Distance a non-line player keeps from the nearest enemy when not moving to help someone: strikers and controllers just inside 20' (6.1 m, their Verbals and Magic Balls), medics and enchanters farther back or near their line, archers well out of melee.

behind_line_m.why: How far behind their own fighting front (the median of their line fighters near the front) a non-line player stays, whatever their preferred distance.

crowd_penalty_seconds.why: When a line fighter picks the enemy to charge (the one it can reach soonest), each teammate already fighting or running at an enemy adds this many seconds to that enemy's time: fighters spread out rather than all piling on one, but a close enemy still draws a second attacker.

caster_priority_seconds.why: A caster, healer or archer counts as this many seconds closer when a line fighter picks whom to charge (Phase 1's caster weight: fighters slightly prefer reachable casters).

reach_horizon_seconds.why: For situational utilities, which may not draw random numbers: the chance a teammate or enemy is 'in range soon' is 1 in range and falls linearly to 0 at what a run covers in this time beyond it.
